---
title: "The Roles in the Kickoff Meeting"
subtitle: "Shared handout for all participants"
pagetitle: "The Roles in the Kickoff Meeting"
---

::: {.hint}
**Everyone gets this.** Here are all the people sitting around the table in the kickoff
meeting for the »LernSpur« platform – with what is **publicly** known about them. You're
all on a **first-name basis** (you know each other from earlier meetings).
In addition, everyone receives a **personal, confidential card** with their *own* goals
and interests. **You do not show this card to the others** – what the others really want
is something you find out in conversation.
:::

::: {.cards}

::: {.card .rse}
<span class="badge">Robin · RSE / software coordination</span>


### Robin — RSE / Software Coordination


<p class="tagline">"I'm supposed to coordinate this – but I can't give orders to anyone here."</p>

* hired at the chair 3 months ago, holds a master's in Research Software Engineering
* is meant to turn the scattered files of the »LernSpur« study into a **sustainable,
  FAIR-compliant platform**
* has **no** authority to give orders to the others
* **leads the kickoff meeting**
* core interest: a viable, maintainable platform
:::

::: {.card .pi}
<span class="badge">Petra · PI / chair</span>

### Petra (Prof. Dr. Barn) — PI / Chair Holder

<p class="tagline">"I'm thrilled about this – just tell me how I can help you make it happen!"</p>

* heads the chair and the »LernSpur« project
* enthusiastic about the idea; wants to publish and share research results
* brought Robin on board and **has the RSE's back**
* cares deeply about the **conference in 8 weeks**
* core interest: a visible success carried by everyone together
:::

::: {.card .domain}
<span class="badge">Mara · education research</span>

### Mara (Dr. Melis) — Education Researcher / Postdoc

<p class="tagline">"You can just tell, surely – just show me the classes that stand out."</p>

* postdoc in empirical education research, knows the data best in terms of content
* wants to advance her own research and pull analyses out of the data
* little software-engineering knowledge, tends to phrase her wishes loosely
* depends on the platform
* core interest: quickly analysable data
:::

::: {.card .hiwi}
<span class="badge">Tobi · student assistant</span>

### Tobi (Tobias) — Student Assistant

<p class="tagline">"Sure, I'll do that … what exactly did you mean again?"</p>

* 4th semester, employed 10 h/week, learned to program mostly from YouTube
* is meant to support Robin and learn along the way
* motivated but inexperienced; availability fluctuates
* core interest: contributing something and learning
:::

::: {.card .partner}
<span class="badge">Sabine · partner school (optional)</span>

### Sabine (Ms. Korter) — Teacher & Contact at a Partner School

<p class="tagline">"What's actually in it for *me* that we're taking part in this?"</p>

* teacher at one of the 14 partner schools, contact person for the study
* her classes supply data (app usage, questionnaires, videos)
* keeps an eye on the benefit for her pupils and on data protection
* barely familiar with everyday research and software work
* core interest: benefit for the school, data protection
:::

:::

::: {.hint}
**Two goals at once.** Everyone at the table shares one **big goal**: that »LernSpur«
succeeds and the meeting ends with a viable plan. Alongside that, everyone has a
**personal goal** – it's on the confidential card and is sometimes at odds with the
others'. It's exactly this tension that makes the game.
:::

::: {.hint}
**How it runs:** Robin opens the meeting. The aim of the round is a shared, **realistic**
plan for the first few weeks. Everyone brings their own interests into it – but the time
until the conference is tight, and not everything will fit. Negotiate until you have a
package everyone can get behind.
:::
